title: 5. Draw the Mini Library ERD
description: Adapted from Week 4 Practical, page 1. Complete this crow’s-foot modeling exercise, then reveal the reference solution below.
brief: Draw a crow’s-foot ERD without answer choices. Include attributes, primary and foreign keys, relationship verbs, and minimum and maximum participation at both ends.

Every member has a unique Member ID and may have zero or many loans. Each loan belongs to exactly one member. Every book title has a unique Book ID and one or more physical copies. Each copy has its own Copy ID and belongs to exactly one title. Every loan refers to one physical copy. A copy may be loaned many times over its lifetime. Assume a new copy may have no loan history. Record borrowed, due and return dates; return date is empty until the copy is returned.
Below the ERD, write the borrowing limits stated in BR7, BR9 and BR10.

solution.title: Reveal model ERD
solution.diagram:
MEMBER       ||────────o{  LOAN       records
BOOK_TITLE   ||────────|{  BOOK_COPY  has
BOOK_COPY    ||────────o{  LOAN       appears in
solution.legend: || exactly one; o{ zero or many; |{ one or many. Read the marks at the opposite end from the entity you start with.
entities: LOAN: LoanID (PK; added for this model), MemberID and CopyID (FKs, required), BorrowDate, DueDate, ReturnDate (nullable).
solution.activeLoanLimits: A copy may have at most one active loan and cannot be borrowed while already on loan. A member may borrow at most three copies at once. ReturnDate stays empty until the copy is returned.
solution.references: Week 4 Practical ERD, p. 1: Mini Library business rules BR1–BR10. Week 3 ER modelling, p. 4: crow’s-foot notation. The practical gives the rules, not a completed diagram; LoanID is a model choice.
